items.title: Bill Mays interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 5, 2025
items.q: I got the gig with Gerry Mulligan immediately and got a chance to play with Al Cohn and Bob Brookmeyer and the Vanguard band

ctx.x: Did you have to sell your parents on this career path?

Well I tried. My father wanted me to be a minister. And I wanted to be a musician. And it was very meaningful that years and years later my dad went to a concert in Italy where I was playing with Gerry and at the end of the concert he said, “I always wanted you to be a minister and you became one in your music and how you touch people.” And that was a wonderful moment. © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-
I bet. Speaking of wonderful moments, your move up to Los Angeles, can you recall the feeling of perhaps nervousness, anticipation the first time you did a significant studio date?
